top_story: Netanyahu’s public rejection on 9 August of a US-backed Gaza ceasefire plan, including any Israeli withdrawal before Hamas disarms, exposed a sharp break with Washington and signaled that the war’s military logic still outweighs diplomatic pressure despite mounting regional costs. Those costs are spreading most visibly in Yemen, where Houthi missile and drone strikes escalated from mass casualties among government troops on 7 August to renewed attacks on al-Makha and its commercial port by 10 August, deepening insecurity along a vital Red Sea corridor and compounding civilian economic strain. In the Palestinian arena, Israel’s rare indictment of settler Yinon Levy over the killing of activist Awdah Hathaleen stands against the far more entrenched pattern reflected in the delayed confirmation of detainee Ihab Diab’s death and his family’s allegations of torture. The overall picture is of limited legal accountability and failing diplomacy reinforcing a wider cycle in which armed actors retain initiative while civilians absorb the consequences.
